title: How to Switch Energy Supplier: UK Guide & Rights
description: How to switch gas and electricity supplier in the UK: how long it takes, cooling-off rights, exit fees, and switching with debt or a prepayment meter.
intro: Switching is free, your supply never goes off, and your new supplier does almost all the work. Here’s what happens and what your rights are.

image.alt: An electricity pole silhouetted against a sunset

cardText: Timeline, cooling-off rights, exit fees and switching with debt.

sections.html:
1. Choose a tariff and sign up with the new supplier (or through a comparison site).
  2. The new supplier contacts your old one. You don’t need to.
  3. You have a 14-day cooling-off period to change your mind.
  4. Give meter readings on the switch day (smart meters send them automatically).
  5. Your old supplier sends a final bill. Any credit should be refunded.

Most switches complete within a few working days of the cooling-off period, and your gas and electricity stay on throughout: the pipes and wires don’t change.

• No exit fees in the last 49 days of a fixed tariff.
  • Prepayment with debt: you can usually switch with up to £500 of debt per fuel (£1,000 dual fuel), which moves to the new supplier.
  • Credit refunds: your old supplier should refund credit after the final bill.
  • Renters: if you pay the energy bills, you can usually switch, but check your tenancy agreement.

Sources: Citizens Advice: energy supply.

sections.h2: When switching might not be right
sections.html: If your fixed deal is cheaper than anything available now, staying put may be best. If you owe your supplier money on a credit meter, you may need to clear the debt before you can leave. If you’re struggling, talk to your supplier about a payment plan and see our grants and support guide.

faqs.q: How long does it take to switch energy supplier?
faqs.a: Usually a few working days after the 14-day cooling-off period, unless you ask to switch sooner. Your supply is never interrupted.

faqs.q: Do I need to tell my old supplier?
faqs.a: No. Your new supplier arranges the switch. Just give accurate meter readings on the switch date.

faqs.q: Can I switch if I’m in debt to my supplier?
faqs.a: Prepayment customers can usually switch with up to £500 of debt per fuel. Credit meter customers often need to repay first. Ask your supplier for help if you’re struggling.
